rituals.name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.ritual_name: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.unique_game_move: Touch Name Pair, follow the moves, and finish on Tag Driver.
rituals.recognition_cue: Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling is a tiny mind game for the moment when several feelings have merged into one heavy mass.
rituals.situation: Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling is a tiny mind game for the moment when several feelings have merged into one heavy mass.
rituals.immediate_need: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.challenge: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling is a tiny mind game for the moment when several feelings have merged into one heavy mass.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

GAME MOVE
Touch Name Pair, follow the moves, and finish on Tag Driver.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

⚡ DONE — Complete Tag Driver, then return to your day.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Name Pair, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.

rituals.plain:
CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING

TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Change One Thing, Watch One Feeling is a tiny mind game for the moment when several feelings have merged into one heavy mass.

GOAL
Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

GAME MOVE
Touch Name Pair, follow the moves, and finish on Tag Driver.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.

⚡ DONE — Complete Tag Driver, then return to your day.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Name Pair, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Swap Variable, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Tag Driver, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The old reaction loses a little speed before Tag Driver.

📸 MY RESULT
“The feeling wasn't one giant thing; it had parts.”

FORMULA FLOW
Name Pair → Hold Scene → Swap Variable → Tag Driver

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Identity may be wearing several visible coats.

GAME MOVE
Start at Move Body. Stop at Place Like. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Move Body — Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease.
2. Ask Change — At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
3. Dont Discard — Do not discard any layer.
4. Place Like — Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action.

⚡ FINISH — Place Like closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Move Body, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Dont Discard, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Place Like, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.

rituals.immediate_need: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

PLAY TIME

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

GAME MOVE
Start with Picture Appears. When Hold Conclusions appears, the round is over.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES? // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief.

⚡ END MOVE — Hold Conclusions. No second lap.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Just before you start Picture Appears, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Ask Claims, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Hold Conclusions, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.

GAME MOVE
Start at Pick Word and keep going only until Jump Letter.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Jump Letter is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Pick Word, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Flash Image, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Jump Letter, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.

📸 MY RESULT

GOAL

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Name Conditions first, Keep Responsibility last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Name Conditions — Review one action and name its conditions: intention, habit, body capacity, other people, tools, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Place Yourself — Place yourself among these causes rather than above them.
3. Keep Responsibility — Keep responsibility for your contribution while releasing sole authorship.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Keep Responsibility, you are done.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Read Order and release the exercise.

rituals.text_plain:
PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER

TRIGGER
Urges, impulses & cravings

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
If several feelings have merged into one heavy mass, Put The Feelings Back In Order turns the mental noise into one playable move.

GOAL
Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.

GAME MOVE
Play from Name Mix to Read Order. Treat the last move as the finish line.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Read Order and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Name Mix, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Link Cue, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Read Order, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The pattern becomes easier to spot before you commit to Read Order.

📸 MY RESULT
“The feeling wasn't one giant thing; it had parts.”

FORMULA FLOW
Name Mix → Find First → Link Cue → Read Order

rituals.name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
rituals.ritual_name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Throwaway as the doorway and Continue Clean as the exit.
rituals.recognition_cue: When good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless, Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.situation: When good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless, Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.immediate_need: A throwaway mistake can make the blank page lose its authority.
rituals.challenge: A throwaway mistake can make the blank page lose its authority.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
When good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless, Make The First Move Deliberately Wrong makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A throwaway mistake can make the blank page lose its authority.

GAME MOVE
Use Throwaway as the doorway and Continue Clean as the exit.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Throwaway — Open a private sandbox and Notice your mental picture THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Create one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy sentence, rough title, ugly Imagine, or incomplete outline.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise save the corrected fragment and stop cleanly.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Continue Clean is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Throwaway, feel where your body is supported for one moment.

rituals.trigger_play_time:

Ally Or Saboteur? is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Ask Thought opens it; Thank Warning closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ALLY OR SABOTEUR? // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real?
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward?
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Thank Warning, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Ask Thought, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Leave Me, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Thank Warning, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.

📸 MY RESULT

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE SUSTAINABLE MIDDLE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest.
2. Find Area — Find the area swinging between too much and too little.
3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks.
4. Choose Smallest — Choose the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Choose Smallest and leave the game there.

rituals.name: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Take Event. Stop at Try Construction. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.recognition_cue: The Waking Dream Check catches the moment when someone else's life has become the ruler for yours and gives you another route.
rituals.situation: The Waking Dream Check catches the moment when someone else's life has become the ruler for yours and gives you another route.
rituals.immediate_need: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
rituals.challenge: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Comparison & rejection

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
The Waking Dream Check catches the moment when someone else's life has become the ruler for yours and gives you another route.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.

GAME MOVE
Start at Take Event. Stop at Try Construction. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE WAKING DREAM CHECK // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Take Event — Take one rigid reading of an event.
2. Compare Dream — Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Identify Facts — Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed.
4. Try Construction — Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes.

⚡ FINISH — Try Construction closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Take Event, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Identify Facts, replace “definitely” with an honest percentage.
3. When you reach Try Construction, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.

🎮 STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Identify Image — Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Redirect is your cue to stop.

Action avoidance & procrastination

about 90 seconds

Do Not Replace The Last Thought gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Wait Thought; stop the moment you complete Count Gap.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Count Gap be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Wait Thought, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Rest Duration, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Count Gap, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Diversity need not become division.

GAME MOVE
Enter through Contrasting; leave as soon as you reach Let Difference. One pass is enough.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DIFFERENCE INSIDE ONE FIELD // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Contrasting — Notice two contrasting experiences—pleasant and painful, self and other, sound and silence.
2. Hold Distinct — Hold their distinct qualities without merging them.
3. Include Shared — Then include the shared field in which both are present.
4. Let Difference — Let difference remain vivid without translating it into separation.

⚡ DONE — Complete Let Difference, then return to your day.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Contrasting, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Include Shared, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Let Difference, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Diversity need not become division.

Experience partly inherits the meaning that organises it.

GAME MOVE
Take the shortest route: Choose Event → the middle moves → Act Lens.

🎮 CHANGE ONE LENS, WATCH THE WORLD // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Choose Event — Choose a current event and Picture the lens being used.
2. Replace Plausible — Replace it with one plausible alternative—not a positive slogan.
3. Act Lens — Spend five minutes acting from the alternate lens and observe changes in body, attention, and available choices.

⚡ END MOVE — Act Lens. No second lap.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Choose Event, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Replace Plausible, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Act Lens, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: Experience partly inherits the meaning that organises it.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
At Act Lens, you have at least one option the first reaction did not show you.

“I just stopped circling and found the next useful point.”

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.

GAME MOVE
Open at Start Brief; close at Test Feasibility. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Start Brief — Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them.
2. Include Conventional — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility.
3. Test Feasibility — Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Test Feasibility be enough.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE REVERSIBLE DOOR // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Find Smallest — Find the smallest action that tests the direction and can be undone: trial, prototype, conversation, temporary booking, one-week schedule.
2. Name Exit — Name the exit cost and the fact the step could reveal.
3. Choose Door — Choose the door that returns with data.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Choose Door and leave the game there.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EMPTY THE MENTAL COUNTERTOP // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Question Promise — Catch every task, question, promise, and loose obligation into one trusted place.
2. Dont Organise — Do not organise while emptying.

4. Choose Physical — Choose only the first physical action.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Choose Physical is your cue to stop.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Relationship care does not require surrendering the point.

GAME MOVE
Play from Remove Attacks to Edit Delivery. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Remove Attacks — Remove attacks from your wording.
2. Validate Understandable — Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
3. Keep Core — Keep your core message unchanged.
4. Edit Delivery — Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Edit Delivery and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SELF-RESPECT CHECKSUM // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Respond Verify — Before responding, verify four conditions: fair to both sides; no apology for merely existing or setting a limit; aligned with your values; completely truthful.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Speak Extra and leave the game there.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Dont Know to Leave Motive.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Dont Know — Picture three separate statements: what they did; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention.
2. Base — Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact.
3. Leave Motive — Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it.

⚡ FINISH — Leave Motive closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Before you begin Dont Know, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Base, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Leave Motive, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE FOUR-PART LIMIT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. State Triggering — State the triggering condition, your limit, the action you will take, and when you will take it.
2. Remove Threats — Remove threats that depend on the other person changing.
3. Practise Line — Practise the line once at speaking volume, then prepare the consequence before delivery.

⚡ END MOVE — Practise Line. No second lap.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start State Triggering, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Remove Threats, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Practise Line, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: A boundary becomes real when follow-through is inside your control.

GOAL

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Catch Sentence opens it; Choose Behaviour closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Choose Behaviour, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Catch Sentence, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Possibility, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Choose Behaviour, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.

1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Choose Behaviour, you are done.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Catch Sentence, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Possibility, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Choose Behaviour, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The first interpretation feels less final when you reach Choose Behaviour.

📸 MY RESULT
“I separated what was said from what I added to it.”

FORMULA FLOW
Catch Sentence → Replace Possibilities → Possibility → Choose Behaviour

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

GAME MOVE
Begin with See The Person. Move straight through to Wait—no extra analysing.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT. // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Wait and leave the game there.

rituals.plain:
SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.

TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Say It In Your Mind. Do Not Send It. makes the invisible part of the pattern easier to catch.

GOAL
Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

GAME MOVE
Begin with See The Person. Move straight through to Wait—no extra analysing.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT. // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Wait and leave the game there.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Give yourself one second before See The Person: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
2. At Do Not Edit, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Wait, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Let this be the line you keep: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You notice the pull of the old pattern and can still choose Wait.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”

FORMULA FLOW
See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait

rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Place Chairs. Stop at Dont And. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.recognition_cue: When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Two Chairs, No Telepathy gives you something concrete to do with the moment.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Two Chairs, No Telepathy gives you something concrete to do with the moment.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

GAME MOVE
Start at Place Chairs. Stop at Dont And. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Dont And — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.

⚡ FINISH — Dont And closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Place Chairs, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Switch Chair, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Dont And, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
When the old reaction is running before you notice it, Two Chairs, No Telepathy gives you something concrete to do with the moment.

GOAL
Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

GAME MOVE
Start at Place Chairs. Stop at Dont And. Let the middle do the work.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Dont And — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.

⚡ FINISH — Dont And closes the round.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Place Chairs, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Switch Chair, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Dont And, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can reach Dont And with more choice than you had at Place Chairs.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”

FORMULA FLOW
Place Chairs → Speak Position → Switch Chair → Dont And

rituals.title: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
rituals.name: MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD
rituals.unique_game_move: Start at Say Alarm and keep going only until Keep Signal.
rituals.recognition_cue: Move The Heaviest Word is for the moment when your mind keeps circling without finding anything new—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.situation: Move The Heaviest Word is for the moment when your mind keeps circling without finding anything new—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.immediate_need: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.challenge: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Body-state misreading

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Move The Heaviest Word is for the moment when your mind keeps circling without finding anything new—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.

GAME MOVE
Start at Say Alarm and keep going only until Keep Signal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MOVE THE HEAVIEST WORD // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Say Alarm — Choose the exact alarm sentence and shorten it to seven words or fewer.
2. Shift Stress — Say it quietly several times, moving emphasis to one different word per round. Keep pitch and speed comfortable.
3. Find Weight — Notice which emphasis changes the meaning or body response most. Focus only on that word.
4. Keep Signal — Keep the weighted word as information; stop the repetitions without debating the whole sentence.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Keep Signal is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Say Alarm, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Find Weight, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Keep Signal, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Move the emphasis and find where the sentence keeps its weight.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can stop at Keep Signal instead of feeding the pattern one more lap.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped circling and found the next useful point.”
rituals.formula_flow: Say Alarm → Shift Stress → Find Weight → Keep Signal

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A forecast should lose influence when its decision window closes.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Picture Prediction to Remove Vote.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, Imagine a line through the forecast and Picture EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.

⚡ FINISH — Remove Vote closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Before you begin Picture Prediction, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Imagine Line, find one fact that does not fit the loudest story.
3. When you reach Remove Vote, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: A forecast should lose influence when its decision window closes.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. After — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: where you are, what year it is, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with ‘That ended; this moment is different.’.

⚡ END MOVE — Finish Moment. No second lap.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TODAY’S FURTHEST USEFUL HORIZON // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

rituals.unique_game_move: Run the sequence once. Make Columns opens it; Perform closes it.
rituals.recognition_cue: Three Selves, Three Jobs is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.situation: Three Selves, Three Jobs is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.immediate_need: Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.
rituals.challenge: Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Three Selves, Three Jobs is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Make Columns opens it; Perform closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Make Columns — Make columns for PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Complete Actions — Put completed actions under past, available repair under present, and prevention plans under future.
3. Cross Out — Cross out any item assigned to the wrong self.
4. Perform — Perform only one present-column task now.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Perform, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Make Columns, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Cross Out, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Perform, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.

📸 MY RESULT

Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Three Selves, Three Jobs is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

GOAL
Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Make Columns opens it; Perform closes it.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Make Columns — Make columns for PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Complete Actions — Put completed actions under past, available repair under present, and prevention plans under future.
3. Cross Out — Cross out any item assigned to the wrong self.
4. Perform — Perform only one present-column task now.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Perform, you are done.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Make Columns, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Cross Out, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Perform, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Perform, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

FORMULA FLOW
Make Columns → Complete Actions → Cross Out → Perform

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.

GAME MOVE
Touch Picture, follow the moves, and finish on Choose Behaviour.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE LIFE RETURNED TEST // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.

⚡ DONE — Complete Choose Behaviour, then return to your day.

rituals.mission: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.
rituals.game_move: Touch Picture, follow the moves, and finish on Choose Behaviour.
rituals.how_to_play:
🎮 THE LIFE RETURNED TEST // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.

⚡ DONE — Complete Choose Behaviour, then return to your day.
rituals.power_up_1: At the start of Picture, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
rituals.power_up_2: At Small, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach Choose Behaviour, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The exercise gives you enough room to make Choose Behaviour intentional.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped circling and found the next useful point.”
rituals.formula_flow_raw: Picture → Small → Choose Behaviour

GOAL

Begin where it says Describe Event; stop the moment you complete Distance.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Describe Event — Say the event once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Distance be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Describe Event, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Return Person, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Distance, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Third-Person Ownership Test gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

GOAL
Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Describe Event; stop the moment you complete Distance.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Describe Event — Say the event once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Distance be enough.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Describe Event, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Return Person, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Distance, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can finish at Distance even if the original thought has not completely disappeared.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Read Action is your cue to stop.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ONE WORD, ONE BREATH, RELEASE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Choose Temporary — Choose a temporary word that holds the issue: betrayal, pressure, uncertainty, loss.
2. Say During — Say it once during a natural breath, feel its weight, and let the word leave with the breath’s end.
3. Dont Replace — Do not replace it with a second Name for thirty seconds.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Dont Replace, you are done.

rituals.name: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
rituals.unique_game_move: Open at Hold In Your Mind Versions; close at Dont Rewrite. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.recognition_cue: Capture The Model’S Miss catches the moment when the past looks obvious only because you know the ending and gives you another route.
rituals.situation: Capture The Model’S Miss catches the moment when the past looks obvious only because you know the ending and gives you another route.
rituals.immediate_need: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
rituals.challenge: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urgency & decision pressure

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Capture The Model’S Miss catches the moment when the past looks obvious only because you know the ending and gives you another route.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.

GAME MOVE
Open at Hold In Your Mind Versions; close at Dont Rewrite. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Hold In Your Mind Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, Keep both versions verbatim.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy.
4. Dont Rewrite — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original forecast.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Dont Rewrite be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Hold In Your Mind Versions, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Name Miss, replace “definitely” with an honest percentage.
3. When you reach Dont Rewrite, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.

You reach Dont Rewrite with a clearer distinction between the reaction and the response.

📸 MY RESULT
“I judged the old choice using what I knew then—not what I know now.”

rituals.title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.name: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.unique_game_move: One round only: enter at Pin Forecast, finish at Update Odds.
rituals.recognition_cue: If fear is making a possibility feel like a certainty, Make Fear Name A Deadline turns the mental noise into one playable move.
rituals.situation: If fear is making a possibility feel like a certainty, Make Fear Name A Deadline turns the mental noise into one playable move.
rituals.immediate_need: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.challenge: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Catastrophic prediction

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
If fear is making a possibility feel like a certainty, Make Fear Name A Deadline turns the mental noise into one playable move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A warning must become testable before it can command you.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Pin Forecast, finish at Update Odds.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Pin Forecast — Rewrite the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the forecast a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence from 0 to 100 before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Update Odds and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Pin Forecast, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Score Odds, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
3. When you reach Update Odds, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: A warning must become testable before it can command you.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The pattern becomes easier to spot before you commit to Update Odds.

📸 MY RESULT
“Fear gave me certainty. Evidence gave me odds.”
rituals.formula_flow: Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE

TRIGGER
Catastrophic prediction

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
If fear is making a possibility feel like a certainty, Make Fear Name A Deadline turns the mental noise into one playable move.

GOAL
A warning must become testable before it can command you.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Pin Forecast, finish at Update Odds.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Pin Forecast — Rewrite the fear as one visible or audible forecast—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the forecast a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence from 0 to 100 before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Update Odds and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Pin Forecast, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Score Odds, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
3. When you reach Update Odds, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: A warning must become testable before it can command you.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The pattern becomes easier to spot before you commit to Update Odds.

📸 MY RESULT
“Fear gave me certainty. Evidence gave me odds.”

FORMULA FLOW
Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds

Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Keep Observations first, Compare Action last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Re — Re-run them under three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the next action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Compare Action, you are done.

1. When you arrive at Keep Observations, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Identify Action, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
3. When you reach Compare Action, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

rituals.how_to_play:
🎮 SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed.
2. Re — Re-run them under three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the next action it recommends.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Compare Action, you are done.
rituals.power_up_1: When you arrive at Keep Observations, press both feet down for three seconds.
rituals.power_up_2: At Identify Action, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach Compare Action, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Compare Action, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“I put the missing context back into the picture.”
rituals.formula_flow_raw: Keep Observations → Re → Identify Action → Compare Action

rituals.ritual_name: KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY
rituals.unique_game_move: Let Hold Trigger begin the game. Let Let Central end it.
rituals.recognition_cue: Keep The Threat, Add The Periphery is for the moment when your attention has narrowed until only one thing is visible—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.situation: Keep The Threat, Add The Periphery is for the moment when your attention has narrowed until only one thing is visible—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.immediate_need: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.
rituals.challenge: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Keep The Threat, Add The Periphery is for the moment when your attention has narrowed until only one thing is visible—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.

GAME MOVE
Let Hold Trigger begin the game. Let Let Central end it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Hold Trigger — Hold the trigger at a tolerable centre.
2. Look Away — Without looking away, name five simultaneous peripheral details—colour, distance, movement, light, geometry.
3. Let Central — Let central and surrounding information coexist until the scene feels larger than the alarm.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Let Central and leave the game there.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Give yourself one second before Hold Trigger: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
2. At Look Away, find one fact that does not fit the loudest story.
3. When you reach Let Central, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.

rituals.plain:
KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY

TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Keep The Threat, Add The Periphery is for the moment when your attention has narrowed until only one thing is visible—before the reaction gets to choose for you.

GOAL
Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.

GAME MOVE
Let Hold Trigger begin the game. Let Let Central end it.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 KEEP THE THREAT, ADD THE PERIPHERY // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Hold Trigger — Hold the trigger at a tolerable centre.
2. Look Away — Without looking away, name five simultaneous peripheral details—colour, distance, movement, light, geometry.
3. Let Central — Let central and surrounding information coexist until the scene feels larger than the alarm.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Let Central and leave the game there.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Give yourself one second before Hold Trigger: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
2. At Look Away, find one fact that does not fit the loudest story.
3. When you reach Let Central, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Danger loses monopoly when neutral data re-enters vision.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can get from Hold Trigger to Let Central without adding another story on top.

📸 MY RESULT
“I widened the frame and found what the tunnel had hidden.”

FORMULA FLOW
Hold Trigger → Look Away → Let Central

Enter through Choose Object; leave as soon as you reach Select Aperture. One pass is enough.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ZOOM LENS TRAINING // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Choose Object — Choose an object.
2. Spend — Spend ten seconds on one tiny feature, ten on the object and nearby context, and ten on the whole visual field.
3. Repeat Shift — Repeat in reverse.
4. Select Aperture — Select the aperture that best fits the actual task.

⚡ DONE — Complete Select Aperture, then return to your day.

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Vivid Is Not Important catches the moment when one thing has hijacked your attention and gives you another route.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Score Information to Allocate Attention.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Score Information — Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
2. Pay Felt — A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the Name.
3. Allocate Attention — Allocate attention to decision impact instead.

⚡ FINISH — Allocate Attention closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Score Information, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Pay Felt, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Allocate Attention, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 GROUNDING ANCHOR RELAY // PLAY

2. Add Controlled — Add controlled variety to the desired task instead: change order, tool, location, soundtrack, colour, or challenge.
3. Keep Goal — Keep the goal constant while refreshing the route.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Keep Goal be enough.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.

Start at Hold In Your Mind Level. Stop at Make Decisions. Let the middle do the work.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Hold In Your Mind Level — At three intervals, Keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
2. Add Action — Add the action impulse at each point.
3. Make Decisions — Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.

⚡ FINISH — Make Decisions closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Before you begin Hold In Your Mind Level, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Add Action, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Make Decisions, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE FEELING UNDER THE FEELING ABOUT IT // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Name Emotion — Name the first emotion and its trigger.
2. Finish About — Then finish: ‘About feeling this, I feel…’ Locate each in a different body area or colour.
3. State Needs — Offer the primary state what it needs before addressing shame, anger, or fear about having it.

⚡ END MOVE — State Needs. No second lap.

🎮 HALF-SPEED THE FIRST MOVE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

rituals.unique_game_move: Give yourself one clean run: Estimate Contribution first, Stop Blaming last.
rituals.recognition_cue: When your body alarm keeps turning itself up, try Return Each Load To Its Source. It makes the pattern easier to see and harder to obey.

rituals.immediate_need: One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Panic & body alarm

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
When your body alarm keeps turning itself up, try Return Each Load To Its Source. It makes the pattern easier to see and harder to obey.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Estimate Contribution first, Stop Blaming last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 RETURN EACH LOAD TO ITS SOURCE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Estimate Contribution — Name current stressors and estimate each contribution to body alarm.
2. Imagine Arrows — Imagine arrows from the present feeling back to its actual sources.
3. Stop Blaming — Address the largest actionable contributor first; stop blaming the most visible issue for unrelated load.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Stop Blaming, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Estimate Contribution, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Imagine Arrows, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Stop Blaming, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: One problem should not carry the weight of the whole week.

📸 MY RESULT

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

GAME MOVE
Play from Press Equal to Reach Zero. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and notice whether the urge to press returns.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Reach Zero and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. To open Press Equal, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Step Down, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Reach Zero, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use low, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

⚡ DONE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.

🎮 DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use low, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

⚡ DONE — Complete Check Panel, then return to your day.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Read Channels, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Move Dial, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Check Panel, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
A small gap appears between the reaction and what you do at Check Panel.

📸 MY RESULT
“My body sounded an alarm; I didn't have to turn it into danger.”

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Seat Feelings — Name up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Survivor. No second lap.

TRIGGER
Communication & conflict

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Try Find The Move No Feeling Must Betray when the argument is gaining speed faster than clarity. It creates just enough space for a different response.

GOAL
Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.

GAME MOVE
Take the shortest route: Seat Feelings → the middle moves → Choose Survivor.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Seat Feelings — Name up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it.

⚡ END MOVE — Choose Survivor. No second lap.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Seat Feelings, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Clear Board, choose the simplest accurate description of the moment.
3. When you reach Choose Survivor, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
Choose Survivor becomes possible without giving the reaction another full round.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just lowered the heat without giving up my point.”

FORMULA FLOW
Seat Feelings → Vetoes → Clear Board → Choose Survivor

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 OPEN THE IDENTITY PORTFOLIO // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Estimate Much — Name five identities active in your life and estimate how much attention each received this week.
2. Choose Neglected — Choose the neglected role that still matters.
3. Perform — Perform one tiny action from its perspective today—friend, learner, neighbour, artist, caregiver, citizen.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Perform is your cue to stop.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Identity claims must show recent action evidence.

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Name Appears opens it; Replace Identity closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 GLOBAL LABELS NEED THREE RECEIPTS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Name Appears — When ‘I’m lazy,’ ‘I’m unlovable,’ or another global Name appears, demand three specific behaviours from the last month that support it and three that complicate it.
2. Replace Identity — If the evidence is mixed, replace identity with a narrower situational description.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Replace Identity, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Name Appears, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Replace Identity, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Replace Identity, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.
rituals.potency_1: When you arrive at Name Appears, press both feet down for three seconds.
rituals.potency_2: At Replace Identity, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
rituals.potency_3: When you reach Replace Identity, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Identity claims must show recent action evidence.
rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Replace Identity, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“A label was one description, not the whole identity.”
rituals.formula_flow: Name Appears → Replace Identity

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REMOVE THE AUDIENCE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Imagine Nobody — Imagine nobody will see, praise, criticise, repost, or hear about the action.

3. Choose Direct — What would you choose if only direct consequences and values remained?
4. Take Smallest — Take the smallest version privately.

⚡ FINISH — Take Smallest closes the round.

HOOK
Call The Inner Council works best when your mind keeps delaying the first move. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.

GAME MOVE
Start at Give Self and keep going only until Chair.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CALL THE INNER COUNCIL // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Chair — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Chair is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:

2. At Protect Whole, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Chair, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.

2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.
3. Protect Whole — Appoint a chair whose job is to protect the whole system over time.
4. Chair — The chair may combine, delay, or reject proposals, but must acknowledge every need.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Chair is your cue to stop.

rituals.power_up_2: At Protect Whole, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach Chair, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Conflicting parts need coordination, not forced unanimity.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can do Chair while some discomfort is still present.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”
rituals.formula_flow_raw: Give Self → Sentence → Protect Whole → Chair

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MOVE THE MEMORY CAMERA // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Place Memory — Place the memory on a screen with enough visual distance.
2. View Scene — View the scene from above, behind, or beside a compassionate observer.
3. Keep Events — Keep events accurate while changing camera position.
4. Add Resources — Add current-you outside the frame with present resources.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Add Resources be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Right before the first move, Place Memory, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Keep Events, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Add Resources, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: You can preserve facts without re-entering the old viewpoint.

rituals.unique_game_move: Play from End Retell to Restore. Treat the last move as the finish line.

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Pain may be stored without its later survival chapter.

GAME MOVE
Play from End Retell to Restore. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE MEMORY DOES NOT END THERE // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. End Retell — Retell only enough to reach the painful ending.
2. Follow Escape — Then append what actually followed: escape, help, adaptation, learning, regained ability, or today’s status.
3. Dont Invent — Do not invent redemption.
4. Restore — Restore the omitted chronology.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Restore and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS

🎮 POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Imagine Two Sides — Imagine two sides.

⚡ DONE — Complete Use One Resource, then return to your day.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SAY THE SENTENCE HISTORY NEVER RECEIVED // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

GOAL

GAME MOVE
Run the sequence once. Introduce opens it; Keep Words closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Keep Words, you are done.

2. At Name Wrong, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Keep Words, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MATCH THE TASK TO THE BODY’S TEMPERATURE // PLAY
One pass is enough. Follow what is written.

1. Read Body — Read current body alarm as low, medium, or high.
2. Select Work — Select work with matching demand: energising movement for low, steady production for medium, simple contained tasks for high.
3. Reassess — Reassess after one unit and change lanes if needed.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Reassess is your cue to stop.

rituals.name: ENTER THROUGH THE SIDE DOOR
rituals.unique_game_move: Give yourself one clean run: Choose A Side Step first, Let It Lead last.
rituals.recognition_cue: Enter Through The Side Door is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.situation: Enter Through The Side Door is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.immediate_need: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.
rituals.challenge: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Enter Through The Side Door is a tiny mind game for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Choose A Side Step first, Let It Lead last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ENTER THROUGH THE SIDE DOOR // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose A Side Step — Pick a small action beside the main task: open one file before starting the work, put on walking shoes before deciding to walk, or wash one ingredient before cooking.
2. Let It Lead — Start with that small step and let it naturally lead into the main task.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Let It Lead, you are done.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Choose A Side Step, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Let It Lead, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Let It Lead, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.

rituals.potency_3: When you reach Let It Lead, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Resistance may accept a neighbouring move.
rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Let It Lead, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”
rituals.formula_flow: Choose A Side Step → Let It Lead

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Name Task; stop the moment you complete Build Smallest.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Name Task — Name the task’s essential purpose.
2. Remove Feature — Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
3. Build Smallest — Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Build Smallest be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Name Task, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Remove Feature, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Build Smallest, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.

rituals.game_move: Let Choose Small begin the game. Let State Behaviour end it.
rituals.how_to_play:
🎮 PAY THE PROCESS IMMEDIATELY // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Choose Small — Choose a small healthy reward delivered right after the process action, regardless of final result: music, Notice, break, pleasant drink, brief message.
2. State Behaviour — State exactly which behaviour earns it and keep the reward proportionate.

⚡ EXIT — Finish State Behaviour and leave the game there.
rituals.power_up_1: Give yourself one second before Choose Small: soften your jaw and unclench your hands.
rituals.power_up_2: At State Behaviour, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach State Behaviour, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Delayed outcomes train weakly; immediate feedback can bridge the gap.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can get from Choose Small to State Behaviour without adding another story on top.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”
rituals.formula_flow_raw: Choose Small → State Behaviour

Move through the sequence once, from Count Pattern to Follow Contract.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SET THE LIMIT BEFORE THE NEXT TEST // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Count Pattern — Define the behaviour in terms a camera could Keep.
2. Set Threshold — Choose the count, duration, or date that will Notice the limit.
3. Link Consequence — Attach one consequence under your control, such as ending the call, leaving, or changing access.
4. Follow Contract — If the threshold is crossed, follow the contract once without holding a motive trial.

⚡ FINISH — Follow Contract closes the round.

GOAL

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Hold In Your Mind Event — For recent interactions, Keep event, context, frequency, repair attempt, and outcome in separate columns.
2. Look Repetition — Look for repetition and exceptions.
3. Issue Narrow — Issue a narrow conclusion tied to the observed period rather than ‘always’ or ‘never.’.

⚡ END MOVE — Issue Narrow. No second lap.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS

Run the sequence once. Name Contact opens it; Hold Setting closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Hold Setting, you are done.

1. When you arrive at Name Contact, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Lower One, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Hold Setting, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.

rituals.unique_game_move: Open at View They; close at Receive Own. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.recognition_cue: Understand, Then Disagree Cleanly gives you a quick reset for the moment when the old reaction is running before you notice it.

PLAY TIME

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Empathy does not sign the other person’s conclusion.

GAME MOVE
Open at View They; close at Receive Own. Keep it light and literal.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 UNDERSTAND, THEN DISAGREE CLEANLY // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. View They — Summarise their view until they could recognise it.
2. Name Need — Name the need or logic you understand.
3. Say Meaning — Then say exactly where your meaning, value, or decision differs.
4. Receive Own — No ‘but’ inside the summary; disagreement receives its own sentence.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Receive Own be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:

1. Right before the first move, View They, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Say Meaning, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Receive Own, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Empathy does not sign the other person’s conclusion.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”

Emotional reasoning

30–60 seconds

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Return Define, finish at Evaluate.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Return Define — Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
2. Specify — Specify what evidence would show each over time.
3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Evaluate and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Return Define, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Specify, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Evaluate, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

📸 MY RESULT

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SET THE CONTACT DOSE // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose Frequency — Before contact, choose frequency, duration, permitted topics, location, and exit phrase.
2. Start Lowest — Start with the lowest dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
3. Use Body — Review afterward using body and behaviour, not guilt.

⚡ DONE — Complete Use Body, then return to your day.

rituals.text_plain:
